full_judgment: 3. Facts giving rise to the proceedings are as follows: The petitioners in pursuance of Article 7 of President's Order No. 98 of 1972 submitted their returns. The petitioner Manindra Nath in his return claimed in all 33 acres of the entire property as retainable and he surrendered his excess quantity of land being 22.72 acres in Khatian 717 of mouza Hanisanja, P.S. Dacope, District Khulna. When the petitioner was awaiting for acceptance of the said statement, the respondent No. 2 the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Khulna, on the basis of a report from the Sub-Divisionnl Manager, passed an order dated 22.5. 75 for taking possession of 41.51 acres of land by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Bagerhat and for taking action under article 8 of the President's Order No. 98 of 1972 on the ground that the petitioner has made a false statement about the quantity of his land vide annexure 'A'. The petitioner having learnt about the order filed an application for further inquiry and this petition was numbered as Misc. Appeal No. 8 of 1975. It is stated by the petitioner that he did not make any false statement; that the order dated 22. 5. 75 was passed behind the back of the petitioner and there had been no inquiry by the Sub- Divisional Officer, Sub-Divisional Manager, Revenue Officer, or any collector (vide annexure B). On 3.12.75 the respondent No.2 passed an order to take over possession of 187'77 acres of land and to take all further necessary action vide annexure 'C'. Being aggrieved the petitioner preferred an appeal under article (2) of the President's Order before the respondent No. 1 which was marked as case No. 170 of 1975. The said appeal was dismissed and it was held that Manindra Nath Das held and possessed all the lauds and since by law he could not have more than 100 bighas the rest of the excess land would be forfeited to the Government vide annexure 'D'. It is stated by the petitioner that his brother Sachindra and Binapani and Durgarani were never in joint family; that they all submitted their respective returns about the holding of land. The order in annexure 'D' is under challenge.
